notes: IQ-05 round 3 (DEC-034): Luke chose variant A, the top 20. Everything else is config_pilot_2014_2021_base.json.
board: 6 px between bars (C2-2: 22) and name and value text up to 0.78 of the bar height, namescale 1.0, so the text is as large as 20 rows allow (29 px names and values on the 1920 frame).

barend (DEC-038): the bars are wider than in round 2 (the board uses about 70% of the width at the leader's bar end); the leader's value and event label still fit inside the frame on every frame (tests/player/run_tests.js).

flags (DEC-037; DEC-035: today's design of every flag, Luke's decision): each driver's flag from data/rtt-002/driver_nationality.csv (flag_code; primary source Wikipedia's list of Grand Prix winners at revision 1376824402, cross-checked with Wikidata, reports/RTT-002_nationality_comparison.md), drawn from the npm package flag-icons 7.5.0 (MIT; reference/rights_ledger.md; no flag file is committed), in a narrow column just left of the bars, moving with its row. The name is always drawn; the flag is an extra cue. column true keeps the column's space, so switching enabled off leaves the layout unchanged.
event_label (DEC-039): a winner on the board shows the Grand Prix after its value ("92 wins · Portuguese GP"), from the first frame of the race until the next race lands, then fades over 0.3 s.

time_label block (DEC-040): season, Grand Prix and date sit left-aligned at x 820, date on y 1012, in the empty space right of the lower bars; the tests check on every frame that the block overlaps no bar, flag, name, value or event label.

overlays (DEC-035 owner, DEC-042 placement): Luke's emblem (square, gold globe and compass) in a 124 x 124 box in the top-right corner, and a generic unbranded car picture in a 440 x 200 box in the bottom-right corner, its bottom edge at y 950 so it stays above the bottom 130 px that YouTube's player controls can cover (an estimate, see DEC-042). Both are private media and never committed (DEC-006): rtt.js loads kits/rtt-002/local_assets/rtt_logo.png and rtt_car.png if present (git-ignored folder); if a file is missing its box stays empty and the render goes on. The boxes are reserved either way; the tests check that no bar, flag, name, value, event label or time-block text ever enters them.

palette and colour_rule.priority (DEC-041): the 22 top-20 colours from round 2 (every pair at least CIEDE2000 18.2 apart, white names at least 3.2:1), reordered: the first 7 are the bright, light ones (CIELAB lightness and chroma both at least 50 as drawn), then the vivid darker ones, then the muted ones. The drivers who ever reach the top ten choose first, most career wins first, and the 7 bright colours are kept for them. The DEC-023 rule (min CIEDE2000 18 between drivers on screen together) is unchanged.
